title: CompostIQ at a glance
claim: Only the API touches the database. The dashboard, the devices and researchers' own scripts all go through it, each with its own kind of credential.

nodes.title: Dashboard
nodes.desc: Dash, pages built on its server

steps: Owners and researchers use the dashboard. It calls the API from its own server with the user's token, so the browser never sees the token or talks to the API.

A compost device sends batches of readings with its own key. It gets that key by pairing with a 6-digit code, or the owner registers it and copies the key over by hand. `emulator/` plays the device in demos.
The simulator generates a whole composting cycle on a developer's machine and can upload it to `/records` with a device key.
Researchers' own scripts read per-country aggregates with a research key created on the dashboard.
The public website is plain HTML pages, served straight from the repo.
Only the API has the database password. Every rule about who may see or change what is checked there, next to the data.
To estimate a bin's composting stage, the API runs the stage model trained in `ml/` on the bin's temperature and moisture readings.
notes: In production, devices, scripts and the website reach the API through NGINX on one VM, and the dashboard calls it over the VM's loopback address. The production VM diagram shows how.
Three credentials never stand in for each other: a device key only sends readings, a user token only works for its account type, and a research key only reads research data.

legend.accent: the only way to the data
